Work issue #99 (cyc-seattle/isthmia): Directus's first-boot admin creation isn't crash-safe or self-healing in the deploy automation. Full context is in the issue body — short version: directus.ts's DirectusRole/DirectusSchema/DirectusUser all assume Directus's own ADMIN_EMAIL/ADMIN_PASSWORD auto-seed succeeded on first boot; it silently didn't (migrations ran, admin never got created), and there's no retry/self-heal, just a bare 401 that blocks pulumi up from ever completing. Also fix the underlying trigger: packages/substrate's compose project collided on ports 80/443 with the old, never-torn-down packages/portal project during the #97 deploy.

Current live state (don't assume clean): the substrate VM is up, Directus is running and fully migrated, but has zero users/roles — nothing to log into. Fix the code first (self-healing admin bootstrap + port-conflict cleanup), verify against a local Directus container the way directus.ts was originally built and tested, then we'll redeploy for real. Don't hand-patch the live instance again — that's exactly what #99 is trying to eliminate. Before you work on this though, note that the last `pulumi up` failed, so verify current state.

# Work an Issue

End-to-end workflow for taking an isthmia issue from open to merged. This repo uses a **PR flow — direct pushes to `main` are not allowed.** Everything goes through a feature branch and pull request.

**The automation never merges.** A human reviewer approves by merging the PR themselves — that manual merge _is_ the approval. The loop's job is to open the PR, keep CI green, respond to review feedback with revisions, and then clean up once the human has merged.

## Prerequisites

- Working tree is clean (`git status`). If there are unrelated uncommitted changes, ask the user how to handle them before branching.
- On `main` and up to date: `git switch main && git pull`.

## Workflow

### 1. Understand the issue

`gh issue view <N>` (add `--comments` if there's discussion). Restate the goal and the acceptance criteria in a sentence. If the issue is unclear or a duplicate, stop and flag it (see the `triage` skill).

### 2. Plan (only if the issue needs one)

Not every issue needs a plan. **Skip** for small, unambiguous changes (a one-line fix, a doc tweak, an obvious test). **Write a plan** when the issue is complex, ambiguous, architectural, touches multiple packages, or has more than one reasonable approach.

When a plan is warranted:

1. Write it as a comment on the issue — the intended approach, the files/packages affected, and any trade-offs or open questions: `gh issue comment <N> --body "..."` (prefix it clearly, e.g. `## Proposed plan`).
2. Mark the issue for review: `gh issue edit <N> --add-label "plan-review"`.
3. **Wait for a human contributor to approve or amend the plan.** Poll the issue (`gh issue view <N> --json labels,comments`). The human signals:
   - **Approved** — they remove the `plan-review` label (their manual go-ahead). Proceed to step 3.
   - **Changes requested** — they leave a comment. Revise the plan, post the updated version as a new comment, and keep waiting (label stays on).
4. Do **not** start implementing until the plan is approved. Use the same backed-off cadence as the PR loop (step 9) while waiting.

### 3. Create a branch

Branch off `main`, named `<type>/<issue#>-<slug>`, matching the issue's type label:

```sh
git switch -c fix/45-duplicate-events   # bug
git switch -c feat/47-auth-reconcile    # enhancement
git switch -c docs/21-readme-auth        # documentation
```

### 4. Write tests first (for bugs and testable logic)

Reproduce the bug with a failing test before fixing it. Tests live at `packages/<pkg>/test/**/*.test.ts` and run under vitest. Mock the external SDK boundary (Parse, google-spreadsheet, googleapis) — see `packages/gsuite/test/spreadsheet.test.ts` for the pattern. Run just the affected package's tests while iterating: `vitest run packages/<pkg>`.

### 5. Implement

Make the change. Match surrounding style: strict TypeScript, ESM with `.js` import extensions, imperative-capitalized commit subjects. Keep the diff scoped to the issue.

### 6. Verify locally

- Full gate (matches CI): `just ci` (install → build → check → test).
- Faster inner loop: `just check` (treefmt + eslint) and `just test`.
- For behavior that needs real Google/Clubspot access, verify with a manual run where feasible (see CLAUDE.md auth model) or clearly state in the PR what could only be tested via mocks.
- Pre-commit hooks (treefmt, eslint) run on commit — `just check` first avoids surprises.

### 7. Commit

Imperative, capitalized subject matching repo history (no conventional-commit prefixes). Reference the issue in the body:

```sh
git commit -m "Write new event ID back to sheet on recreate" -m "Fixes #45"
```

### 8. Push, open the PR, and request review

```sh
git push -u origin HEAD
gh pr create --fill --base main
```

- Ensure the PR body links the issue with a closing keyword (`Closes #45`) so the merge auto-closes it.
- Request review from the human reviewer(s) so the PR shows up in their queue: `gh pr edit <N> --add-reviewer <login>`.
- Post a short comment making the hand-off explicit: _"Ready for review. Merge it yourself when you're happy — that's the approval. I'll keep CI green and address any review comments."_
- Then enter the automated review loop (step 9).

### 9. Automated review loop (never merges)

Poll the PR on a cadence until the human merges it or closes it. Each cycle, gather state:

```sh
gh pr view <N> --json state,mergeStateStatus,statusCheckRollup,reviews,comments
```

Then act on it:

- **Merged by a human:** `state == "MERGED"` → go to step 10 (cleanup). This is the approval signal.
- **Closed without merging:** `state == "CLOSED"` → stop the loop and report; don't reopen or re-push.
- **CI red / failing checks:** get the failure (`gh run view <run-id> --log-failed`), fix on the branch, commit, push. To be woken when a run finishes rather than polling blindly, run `gh pr checks <N> --watch` in the background.
- **Changes requested or actionable review comments:** address each with commits on the same branch, push, and reply to the threads noting what changed. Don't force-push over review history unless asked. This is a _revision_ — the loop continues.
- **Green and waiting:** nothing to do — the PR is the human's to merge. Wait and re-check.

**Never run `gh pr merge`.** The automation keeps the PR healthy; the human presses merge.

**Cadence (use `ScheduleWakeup`):** while CI is actively running, check on a short interval (a few minutes). While idle waiting for the human to merge, back off to ~20–30 min so you don't burn cycles. Stop looping if the PR is merged or closed.

### 10. Clean up after the human merges

```sh
git switch main && git pull
git branch -d <branch>   # delete the local feature branch (remote branch is deleted at merge time or by GitHub)
```

Confirm the issue closed (the `Closes #N` keyword handles it). Report the merged PR and closed issue back to the user.

## Guardrails

- Never push directly to `main`. **Never merge PRs** — the human reviewer merges manually; that manual merge is the approval. The automation only opens the PR, keeps CI green, and addresses feedback.
- For issues that needed a plan (step 2), don't start implementing until the `plan-review` label is removed (plan approved).
- Keep one issue per branch/PR. If you discover unrelated problems, capture them as new issues (see the `capture` skill) rather than expanding scope.
- If CI keeps failing after a couple of honest fix attempts, or a review asks for something ambiguous, stop the loop and ask the user rather than guessing.

{"body":"## Problem

During the first real deploy of #97 (the people-hub/Directus rollout), Directus's own bootstrap
process ran migrations successfully (107 rows in `directus_migrations`) but never created the admin
user (0 rows in `directus_users`) or the default Administrator role/policy. `DirectusRole` /
`DirectusSchema` / `DirectusUser` (`packages/infrastructure/src/directus.ts`, `people-hub.ts`) all
authenticate as `ADMIN_EMAIL`/`ADMIN_PASSWORD` (the `directus-admin-bootstrap-password` secret) to do
their work via Directus's REST API — with no admin user existing, every one of them fails with a
bare `401 Invalid user credentials`, and `pulumi up` can't proceed at all.

Likely trigger: Directus's `bootstrap` command treats "has `directus_migrations` rows" as "already
installed" and skips admin-seeding on that basis — not "does an admin actually exist." In this
deploy, the substrate VM's `docker compose up -d` partially failed (the new `substrate-caddy-1`
container couldn't bind :80/:443 because the old `portal-caddy-1`/`portal-oauth2-proxy-1`
containers, from a completely separate never-torn-down compose project, were still holding them),
which plausibly interrupted Directus mid-bootstrap — after migrations completed, before
admin-seeding ran. Once that happens, no restart, no re-run of `directus bootstrap`, and no
`pulumi up` retry fixes it: the migrations table already has rows, so Directus always skips the
admin-seed step from then on. Recovery required manually running
`docker exec ... node cli.js users create ...` directly on the box — not reproducible, and not
something anyone should have to do again.

Two separate causes worth fixing:
1. `packages/substrate/deploy/docker-compose.yml`'s project (`substrate`) collided on ports with the
   pre-existing `portal` project from before #97 — nothing tears down the old project when the
   compose project name changes.
2. The Pulumi automation (`directus.ts`'s `DirectusRole`/`DirectusSchema`/`DirectusUser`,
   `people-hub.ts`) has a hard, silent dependency on Directus's own opaque first-boot admin-seeding
   succeeding, with no verification, retry, or self-healing if it doesn't (for this reason or any
   other).

## Fix

- For (1): have the bootstrap script (`substrate-bootstrap.ts`) explicitly stop/remove containers
  from any other compose project sharing the host network ports before bringing up its own, or
  otherwise make the boot idempotent against stale prior projects.
- For (2): make the admin bootstrap self-healing rather than a silent prerequisite — e.g., have
  `directus.ts` check whether login as `ADMIN_EMAIL` succeeds, and if not, create the Administrator
  role/policy + admin user directly via the API (the same way `DirectusUser` already creates other
  users) before the rest of the automation runs. Add a regression test for the login-check/self-heal
  path if one can be written without a live Directus instance (a mocked HTTP layer, matching this
  package's existing test conventions where practical).

## Impact

Without this, any future fresh deploy (or anyone recovering a broken instance) can hit the exact
same dead end: full automation, `pulumi up` included, silently unable to proceed past a `401`, with
the only known fix being manual CLI surgery on the box.","comments":[],"labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDON4Gka88AAAAB5PiTuw","name":"bug","description":"Something isn't working","color":"d73a4a"},{"id":"LA_kwDON4Gka88AAAACqxFGvw","name":"P1","description":"High priority","color":"D93F0B"}],"state":"OPEN","title":"Directus first-boot admin creation isn't crash-safe or self-healing in deploy automation"}

# The substrate VM's whole compose stack: every surface behind the one shared Caddy container,
# routed by hostname. Today that's the cycsail.team portal (gated by oauth2-proxy) and the people
# hub (Directus, its own native Google OIDC login — no oauth2-proxy needed for that surface). Secret
# values come from an env file written at boot from Secret Manager (see cloud-init in
# infrastructure/src/substrate-bootstrap.ts) — nothing sensitive lives in git.
services:
  caddy:
    image: ${CADDY_IMAGE}
    restart: unless-stopped
    environment:
      SITE_DOMAIN: ${SITE_DOMAIN}
      CRM_DOMAIN: ${CRM_DOMAIN}
    ports:
      - "80:80"
      - "443:443"
    volumes:
      - caddy_data:/data
      - caddy_config:/config
    depends_on:
      - oauth2-proxy
      - directus

  oauth2-proxy:
    image: quay.io/oauth2-proxy/oauth2-proxy:v7.6.0
    restart: unless-stopped
    command:
      - --http-address=0.0.0.0:4180
      - --reverse-proxy=true
      # Auth-only in front of Caddy: oauth2-proxy makes the allow/deny decision; Caddy serves.
      - --upstream=static://202
      - --provider=google
      - --redirect-url=https://${SITE_DOMAIN}/oauth2/callback
      - --cookie-domain=${SITE_DOMAIN}
      - --whitelist-domain=${SITE_DOMAIN}
      # Accept any Google account (personal Gmail included); the group check below is the real gate.
      - --email-domain=*
      # Authorization = membership in the all@ group (which nests staff@, volunteers@, …).
      - --google-group=${OAUTH2_PROXY_GOOGLE_GROUP}
      - --google-admin-email=${OAUTH2_PROXY_GOOGLE_ADMIN_EMAIL}
      # Use the VM's own service account (Application Default Credentials via the metadata server)
      # for the Directory API group lookup — no long-lived key file. The substrate SA must have
      # domain-wide delegation for admin.directory.group.readonly (see ../README.md).
      - --google-use-application-default-credentials=true
      - --set-xauthrequest=true
    environment:
      # Shared platform-wide Google OAuth client (substrate.ts) — SSO between this and Directus.
      OAUTH2_PROXY_CLIENT_ID: ${GOOGLE_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID}
      OAUTH2_PROXY_CLIENT_SECRET: ${GOOGLE_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET}
      OAUTH2_PROXY_COOKIE_SECRET: ${OAUTH2_PROXY_COOKIE_SECRET}

  # The people hub. Talks to its own database on the shared Cloud SQL instance over private IP
  # (no Cloud SQL Auth Proxy needed — the VM and Cloud SQL are on the same VPC).
  #
  # Directus 12+ (MSCL-licensed) gates custom/relational permission rules (the $CURRENT_USER-scoped
  # filters the Guardian policy depends on — see docs/people-hub-schema.md) behind a license; CYC
  # has one via Directus's Open Innovation Grant (nonprofit, well under the $5M revenue / 50
  # employee thresholds — see docs/manual-setup.md §6). LICENSE_KEY below is required for the
  # Guardian role to actually work, not just for this version number.
  directus:
    image: directus/directus:12.3.1
    restart: unless-stopped
    environment:
      KEY: ${DIRECTUS_KEY}
      SECRET: ${DIRECTUS_SECRET}
      LICENSE_KEY: ${DIRECTUS_LICENSE_KEY}
      DB_CLIENT: pg
      DB_HOST: ${DIRECTUS_DB_HOST}
      DB_PORT: "5432"
      DB_DATABASE: directus
      DB_USER: directus
      DB_PASSWORD: ${DIRECTUS_DB_PASSWORD}
      ADMIN_EMAIL: ${DIRECTUS_ADMIN_EMAIL}
      ADMIN_PASSWORD: ${DIRECTUS_ADMIN_PASSWORD}
      PUBLIC_URL: https://${CRM_DOMAIN}
      # Native Google OIDC, same shared client as oauth2-proxy above — see
      # docs/manual-setup.md for the one-time OAuth client setup. No oauth2-proxy in front of this
      # surface; Directus enforces its own login + roles.
      AUTH_PROVIDERS: google
      AUTH_GOOGLE_DRIVER: openid
      AUTH_GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID: ${GOOGLE_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID}
      AUTH_GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET: ${GOOGLE_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET}
      AUTH_GOOGLE_ISSUER_URL: https://accounts.google.com
      AUTH_GOOGLE_IDENTIFIER_KEY: email
      AUTH_GOOGLE_ALLOW_PUBLIC_REGISTRATION: "false"

volumes:

Backing the people hub (see [docs/people-hub-schema.md](people-hub-schema.md)). No oauth2-proxy in
front of this surface — Directus authenticates directly via its own native Google OIDC (the shared

> ⚠️ **License note:** the relationship-based permission filters this data model depends on (a
> guardian reading only their own minor's record, e.g. the `Guardian` role's `$CURRENT_USER`-scoped
> rules) are gated behind a Directus license on v12+ (MSCL) — confirmed hands-on while building the
> schema (a fresh, unlicensed v12.3.1 instance rejected any permission with a `permissions` filter
> with `403 custom_permission_rules_enabled is a restricted resource`).
>

> well under the $5M revenue / 50 employee thresholds — free, explicitly includes custom access
> policies, valid one year and renewable). `docker-compose.yml` is pinned to a current `12.x` with
> `LICENSE_KEY` wired in (§3, `directus-license-key`) — set that secret before first boot, and
> renew the grant/license annually.

Everything below is now `pulumi up` — the only genuinely irreducible manual step left is the one
Postgres `GRANT` in §6.1 (it needs a live SQL connection; nothing that runs `pulumi up` has a
network path to Cloud SQL's private IP today). No more `directus schema apply` CLI, no more
first-boot-admin-then-create-my-account dance, no more secret values to invent — `directus-key`,
`directus-secret`, `directus-db-password`, `directus-admin-bootstrap-password`, and
`portal-oauth-cookie-secret` are all Pulumi-generated now (see `randomSecret` in `secret.ts`),
nothing to fill in for them in §3.

### 6.1 Database role — Cloud SQL

Pulumi creates the `directus` Postgres role itself (`postgres.user()` in `database.ts`, via the
Cloud SQL Admin API — no network path to the instance needed for that part) with the generated
`directus-db-password` value. What Pulumi **can't** do: grant that role privileges on the
`directus` database — Postgres 16's tightened default (no public `CREATE` on a fresh database's
`public` schema) means that needs a live SQL connection, and Cloud SQL here is private-IP-only with
no network path from wherever `pulumi up` runs. One remaining manual step:

- [ ] Connect to the `substrate` Cloud SQL instance (`gcloud sql connect substrate --user=postgres`,
      or via a bastion/IAP tunnel) and run:
      `sql
GRANT ALL PRIVILEGES ON SCHEMA public TO directus;
GRANT ALL PRIVILEGES ON DATABASE directus TO directus;
`

      fragility didn't seem worth it for something this narrow. Say so if that trade-off should go
      the other way.)

`infrastructure/src/people-hub.ts` applies the committed
[`packages/people-hub/schema.yaml`](../packages/people-hub/schema.yaml) snapshot
(`DirectusSchema`, via Directus's own `/schema/diff` + `/schema/apply` REST endpoints — going
through the running server's API instead of the CLI also means no restart-for-stale-cache gotcha),
creates the Staff/Coach/Guardian roles (`DirectusRole`), and provisions `ungood@onetrue.name` as a
Staff user via Google OIDC (`DirectusUser` — no password; signing in with that Google account just
works, no bootstrap-admin dance).

      generates it — see above, nothing to do) and Directus to already be reachable at

      won't wait forever. On a truly fresh deploy this is often the _second_ `pulumi up` (first:
      secrets/DB/DNS containers + the VM; you do §6.1's `GRANT` and confirm the VM picked up the

# Manual setup steps

Most of this platform is infrastructure-as-code (Pulumi, in `packages/infrastructure`). A handful of
steps **cannot** be — they live in Google consoles, the Workspace Admin console, or the domain
registrar, or they involve secret _values_ that must never enter git. This doc is the running record
of every such out-of-band step, so setting up a fresh environment (or recovering one) doesn't rely
on memory.

Legend: `[ ]` = to do for a new setup, `[x]` = done for the current production setup (as of this doc).

> Why these can't be code: OAuth "Web application" clients and the **External** consent screen have
> no Terraform/Pulumi resource; domain-wide delegation and Workspace settings live in the Admin
> console and would require super-admin credentials that our access policy deliberately keeps out of
> automation (see [CLAUDE.md](../CLAUDE.md) → Access policy); registrar delegation is at the domain
> registrar; and external credentials (OAuth secrets, third-party logins) are set out of band by
> design — Pulumi declares only the container for those. Internal keys/passwords with no meaningful
> human choice are the exception: Pulumi generates and manages those values directly (see §3).

## Proposed plan

Reproduced the failure locally (fresh Postgres + `directus/directus:12.3.1`, let it fully bootstrap
so an admin exists, then deleted `directus_users`/`directus_roles`/`directus_policies`/`directus_access`
rows while leaving `directus_migrations` intact, then restarted the container). Confirms the "likely
trigger" hypothesis exactly: on restart Directus logs `Database already initialized, skipping install`
and never re-seeds — a bare 401 on `/auth/login` from then on, permanently.

**The originally-proposed fix (self-heal via Directus's own REST API) doesn't work.** I probed every
plausible unauthenticated endpoint against that broken instance (`POST /users`, `POST /roles`,
`GET /roles`, `POST /users/register`) — all `403 FORBIDDEN`. With zero users, Directus's REST API has
no bootstrap escape hatch; every collection is gated even when nothing exists yet. The only thing that
actually worked (confirmed against the same broken container) was `docker exec <container> node cli.js
roles create --role Administrator --admin --app` (prints the new role ID) followed by
`node cli.js users create --email ... --password ... --role <id>` — i.e., exactly the manual recovery
already used, just made repeatable. `node cli.js count directus_users` gives a clean idempotency check
(only self-heal when it's `0`).

So the fix needs container-exec access to the VM, not just HTTP. Proposed shape:

- **New `ssh.ts`**: a small helper that shells out to `gcloud compute ssh <instance> --zone <zone>
  --tunnel-through-iap --command <script>`. Deployers already hold `roles/iap.tunnelResourceAccessor`
  + `roles/compute.osLogin` (`compute.ts`) — no new IAM needed, just the first thing to actually *use*
  that access from Pulumi itself rather than a human's terminal.
- **`directus.ts`**: a `selfHealAdmin(target, adminEmail, adminPassword)` that builds the idempotent
  remote script (count check, then `roles create` + `users create` against the fixed
  `substrate-directus-1` container name — deterministic from the compose project/service names) and
  runs it via `ssh.ts`. Wrap the existing `login()` in a `loginAsAdmin()` used by
  `DirectusSchema`/`DirectusRole`/`DirectusUser`'s create/update paths: try login, on 401 call
  `selfHealAdmin` then retry once, throw a clear combined error if that still fails.
- **`people-hub.ts`**: extend the shared `auth` object with the substrate instance name + zone so it
  flows through the existing `Args` plumbing to all three resource types.
- **`substrate-bootstrap.ts`** (fix 1, the actual trigger): before `pull`/`up -d`, remove any running
  container whose `com.docker.compose.project` label isn't `substrate` — fixes the port 80/443
  collision with the never-torn-down `portal` project from before #97.
- **Tests**: mock `fetch` + mock the new `ssh.ts` module to unit-test `loginAsAdmin`'s three paths
  (healthy login / self-heal-then-succeed / self-heal-then-still-fails) without a live Directus
  instance or VM — matching the mocked-SDK-boundary convention. The remote script itself was verified
  by hand against the local repro above (not something CI can exercise) — noted in the PR.

**Worth flagging explicitly:** this is the first time `pulumi up` gets shell-exec capability against
the VM, not just GCP-API calls — a step up from the existing "one manual `GRANT`" trade-off
(`directus.ts`'s own comment on that one), which was left manual specifically because it wasn't
worth automating for something that narrow. Here the payoff (unblocking the entire
schema/role/user resource chain on any future first-boot flake) seems worth it, but it's a real
change to what deploy automation can do, not just a bigger version of the same thing — flagging per
the access-policy framing in CLAUDE.md rather than assuming it's fine.
PLANEOF

content.text:
I've posted a plan on issue #99 and marked it `plan-review`. Summary of what I found and propose:

**The issue's originally-proposed fix doesn't actually work.** I reproduced the exact failure locally (fresh Directus, wiped the admin user/role while leaving migrations intact, restarted — confirmed it logs `Database already initialized, skipping install` and permanently 401s). I then probed every unauthenticated REST endpoint that could plausibly seed the first admin (`/users`, `/roles`, `/users/register`) — all `403`. With zero users, Directus's API has no bootstrap escape hatch over HTTP.

**What actually works** (verified against the same broken container): `docker exec` into the Directus container and run its CLI (`node cli.js roles create --admin` then `users create`), gated by `node cli.js count directus_users == 0` for idempotency — i.e., automate the exact manual recovery already used.

That means the fix needs a new capability: Pulumi shelling out over IAP SSH to exec commands in the container, not just HTTP calls. That's a real step up from what deploy automation does today (it's only ever made GCP-API/HTTP calls so far), so I stopped before writing code and flagged the trade-off explicitly in the plan rather than assuming it's fine.

Plan is on the issue: https://github.com/cyc-seattle/isthmia/issues/99#issuecomment-5610726807 — new `ssh.ts` helper (using IAP/OS-Login access deployers already have), `selfHealAdmin()` in `directus.ts`, wiring through `people-hub.ts`, plus the separate port-conflict fix in `substrate-bootstrap.ts`, with unit tests mocking `fetch` and the new SSH module.

Let me know if the SSH-exec approach is the right call, or if you'd rather constrain it differently — happy to proceed once you're good with it.
I don't _need_ self healing. If this is just a bug in the first time we ran this thing, we can just wipe it all away and start over.

## Summary

Root-cause fix for #99: the substrate compose stack collided on host ports 80/443 with the
pre-substrate-rename `portal` compose project, which was never torn down. That collision plausibly
interrupted Directus mid-bootstrap during the #97 deploy, before it seeded the admin user/role —
Directus's own install-check is gated on migrations having run, not on an admin actually existing, so
once that happens no restart/retry fixes it (confirmed by reproducing the exact scenario against a
local Directus container — see commit message).

Per discussion on the issue: no self-healing/auto-repair. I initially proposed a self-heal that
recreates the admin via Directus's REST API, but verified locally that's not actually possible (every
write endpoint 403s with zero users — Directus has no unauthenticated bootstrap escape hatch). Since
this looks like a one-time first-deploy bug, the agreed call is to fix the actual trigger (this PR)
and, separately, wipe the currently-broken live Directus state and redeploy clean — not build new
SSH-exec automation for something the trigger fix should prevent from recurring.

Also includes an already-in-progress, independent fix: `getSecretVersionOutput` for the admin
bootstrap password had no `dependsOn` on the secret's own `SecretVersion` write, so the read had no
ordering guarantee against it on a fresh deploy.

## Changes

- `substrate-bootstrap.ts`: cloud-init now removes any running container whose
  `com.docker.compose.project` label isn't this project's own before pulling/starting the stack.
- Extracted the cloud-init string-templating into a new pulumi-free `substrate-bootstrap-script.ts`
  so it's unit testable (the original file's top-level pulumi/GCP resource construction makes it
  unimportable from a plain vitest test).
- `secret.ts` / `people-hub.ts`: thread the `SecretVersion` resource through `randomSecret`'s return
  value and `dependsOn` it when reading the admin bootstrap password back.

## Test plan

- [x] `just ci` (build, format/lint, vitest) passes.
- [x] New unit test (`substrate-bootstrap-script.test.ts`) covers the cleanup-ordering and
      project-name-scoping logic.
- [x] Manually verified the actual cleanup shell logic against real containers on a local Docker
      network (a stale differently-labeled container holding a port gets removed; same-project and
      unrelated containers don't) — not something CI can exercise since it needs a real Docker
      daemon and simulated stale state.
- [x] Manually reproduced the original failure against a local `directus/directus:12.3.1` +
      Postgres container (wiped admin/role/policy rows while leaving migrations intact, restarted —
      confirmed the permanent 401) to confirm the root-cause hypothesis before fixing it.

Closes #99
EOF

- Almost all of that diff (image rebuild/replace, portal-secret deletion, the 5 new `people-hub-*` resources) already exists on plain `main` — it's pre-existing pending work from the earlier failed `pulumi up` attempts, not something our branch introduces.

- Directus is reachable (`/server/ping` → 200), but the VM's own comment in `compute.ts` says changing metadata on an already-running VM does **not** re-run cloud-init — only replacing the VM does. So this `pulumi up` will update the metadata, but won't actually re-trigger the cleanup/bootstrap on the live box.
- That means `pulumi up` will very likely fail at the exact same spot as the last 3 attempts: creating `people-hub-schema` (401, since the live Directus instance still has no admin user — nothing in this deploy touches that).

content.text:
(That last tool call was just me being silly with the tool — ignore it. Here's the actual command, plainly:)

```
! gcloud auth login
```

Run that with the leading `!` so it executes in this session — it'll open a browser login for your `ungood@onetrue.name` account.

While that's pending, here's the exact wipe I'm proposing, so you can sign off on it before I touch anything:

**Plan:**
1. SSH into the `substrate` VM via IAP tunnel (`gcloud compute ssh substrate --zone=... --tunnel-through-iap`) — no public SSH port involved, this is the same access deployers already use.
2. From there, run a throwaway `postgres:16-alpine` container against the VM's Docker socket to connect to the Cloud SQL private IP as the `directus` role, and run:
   ```sql
   DROP OWNED BY directus CASCADE;
   ```
   This drops every table/object the `directus` role has ever created in that database (currently just Directus's own internal system tables — ~107 migrations' worth, no app schema yet since that step never got reached). It does **not** touch the Cloud SQL "database" or "user" objects Pulumi tracks, and doesn't need the Postgres superuser password — just the already-known `directus` role password.
3. Restart the `directus` container (`docker restart substrate-directus-1`) so it reruns its own startup bootstrap against the now-empty database — a genuine fresh install, which I already verified (locally) seeds the admin role/user correctly.
4. Then run `pulumi up` for real (via `just deploy`), which should now get past the `people-hub-schema` step since Directus will actually have an admin to log in as.

Cloud SQL has automated backups + PITR enabled, so this is recoverable even though step 2 is otherwise irreversible. Nothing of real value exists in there yet (0 users, no app data) — but let me know if you'd rather I take a manual backup snapshot first anyway. Confirm and I'll proceed once you're reauthed.
confirm

Hit a real permission wall: `gcloud compute ssh` fails because `ungood@onetrue.name` is an external identity to the `cyccommunitysailing.org` org — OS Login for an external user needs `roles/compute.osLoginExternalUser` granted at the **organization** level, not just the project-level `roles/compute.osLogin` that `compute.ts` currently grants. That's a gap in what's actually wired up, separate from anything this PR touches.

I could work around it by switching to `master@cyccommunitysailing.org` (an org member, so OS Login would just work) — but CLAUDE.md is explicit that `master@` is reserved for super-admin config changes and shouldn't be used for day-to-day dev/deploy, so I don't think I should route around it that way without you saying so.

# Capture an Issue

Turn a problem — from the current conversation or the user's description — into a well-formed GitHub issue in `cyc-seattle/isthmia`.

## Steps

1. **Gather the problem.** Pull details from the conversation or ask the user. A good issue needs: what's wrong or wanted, where in the code (`path:line`), and why it matters.
2. **Check for duplicates first.** `gh issue list --state open --limit 100 --json number,title,labels`. If it overlaps an existing issue, tell the user and offer to comment on / rescope that one instead of filing a new duplicate.
3. **Pick a type label:** `bug`, `enhancement`, `documentation`, or `docker`.
4. **Assign a priority label** using the rubric below.
5. **Write the body** using the template below. Reference concrete files as `path:line`.
6. **Create it:** `gh issue create --title "<imperative title>" --label "<type>,<priority>" --body "$(cat <<'EOF' ... EOF)"`
7. **Report** the issue number and URL back to the user.

## Priority rubric (P0–P3)

- **P0 — Critical:** data integrity/corruption, production broken, or a security-critical hole. Work starts immediately.
- **P1 — High:** a significant bug or friction the user hits regularly, with no safe workaround (e.g. auth/tooling breakage).
- **P2 — Medium:** a real improvement or a bug with a workaround (added tests, hardening, moderate bugs).
- **P3 — Low:** cleanup, docs, polish, low-risk nice-to-haves.

## Body template

Keep it tight. Use `## Problem` always; then `## Fix` (bugs) or `## Proposed changes` / `## Scope` (enhancements); add `## Impact` when the "why" isn't obvious.

```markdown
## Problem

<what's wrong/wanted, with `path:line` references and a code snippet if useful>

## Fix

<concrete change; mention adding a regression test for bugs>

## Impact

<why it matters — omit if self-evident>
```

## Conventions

- **Title:** short, imperative, no priority prefix (priority lives in the label). e.g. "safeCall retries non-retryable errors with a 60s delay".
- Labels already exist: `P0`–`P3`, `bug`, `enhancement`, `documentation`, `docker`. Don't invent new ones without asking.
- For bugs, always note that the fix should include a regression test — tests live in `packages/*/test/**/*.test.ts`.
- Cross-link related issues with `#N` and note dependencies ("land #47 first").

`pulumi up` fails applying the people hub's Directus schema:

but `packages/substrate/deploy/docker-compose.yml` pins `directus/directus:12.3.1`. `DirectusSchema`
(`packages/infrastructure/src/directus.ts`'s `applySchema`, via `POST /schema/diff` +
`POST /schema/apply`) doesn't pass Directus's `force` query parameter, so the version check always
rejects it. This blocks `people-hub-schema` from ever being created — and everything that
`dependsOn` it (`people-hub-staff`/`-coach`/`-guardian` roles, `people-hub-staff-ungood`) with it.

is the very next step in the same dependency chain, so it's effectively still blocking the initial
people-hub deploy from completing.

Most likely just a stale metadata field: `docs/manual-setup.md` §6 notes the schema's permission
filters (the license-gated `$CURRENT_USER` relational rules) were already hand-tested against a real
Directus 12.3.1 instance, so the schema content itself is very likely already compatible — the
`directus: 11.17.4` line looks like it was never updated after the compose file was later pinned to
12.3.1 for the license feature. Bump `packages/people-hub/schema.yaml`'s `directus:` field to
`12.3.1` and re-verify the diff/apply succeeds against a real 12.3.1 instance (not just blindly pass
`force` in `applySchema` — that would permanently mask any future real incompatibility instead of
fixing this one).

assert the version in the schema payload is checked/kept in sync, or at least that a version
mismatch surfaces clearly) — see existing test conventions in `packages/gsuite/test/`.

## Impact

Blocks the people hub's very first successful deploy — the schema/roles/first-staff-user resources
can never be created until this is fixed, regardless of #99 being fixed.

## Summary

One line: bump the recorded version to `12.3.1`. Not passing Directus's `force` bypass instead —
that would permanently mask any future real incompatibility rather than fixing this one, and the
mismatch here really was just a stale field.

content.text:
Found the Directus issue clearly: it's sending `redirect_uri=https://crm.cycsail.team/auth/login/google/callback` to Google, and getting `redirect_uri_mismatch` back — meaning that exact URI was never added to the Google OAuth client's **Authorized redirect URIs** list. That's a manual Google Cloud Console setting (per CLAUDE.md, OAuth clients have no Pulumi resource), and this is the very first time anyone's ever actually tried logging into Directus, so it makes sense nobody's added it yet.

**Fix**: in Google Cloud Console → APIs & Services → Credentials → the shared OAuth client (id starting `841708200159-ojded1kekq22e...`) → add `https://crm.cycsail.team/auth/login/google/callback` to Authorized redirect URIs. That's a console-only change — I can't do it via `gcloud`/Pulumi.

For the portal's 403, I need to check `oauth2-proxy`'s logs to confirm it's the group-membership issue (already a known limitation) rather than something else, but my `gcloud` session needs reauth again:

input.command:
cat > /tmp/pr-app-access-body.md << 'EOF'
## Summary

`DirectusRole` created policies with no `app_access` field. Directus defaults that to `false`
(API-only) — so every role this resource creates (Staff, Coach, Guardian) was silently unusable for
actually signing into the Directus Data Studio, even though authentication itself succeeds. Surfaced
tonight: first real login attempt (Google OIDC as `ungood`, Staff role) got "No App Access" right
after a successful sign-in.

## Change

Made `appAccess` a required field on `DirectusRoleArgs`/`DirectusRoleInputs` (no default — this bug
was exactly a silent-default problem, didn't want to trade one default for another) and set it on
the policy in both `create` and `update`. `people-hub.ts`: `true` for Staff/Coach (real users signing
into the app), `false` for Guardian (no login path yet — will be a future end-user-facing portal, not
the Directus app itself, per its own "No login yet" comment).

## Test plan

- [x] `just ci` passes.
- [x] Verified against a real local Directus 12.3.1 instance: created a policy with no `app_access`
      field (mirroring the bug) and confirmed `/auth/login` succeeds fine (200, valid JWT) but the
      token carries `"app_access":false` — confirms the failure is a Data Studio (app-level) gate on
      an otherwise-successful login, not an auth failure, matching what was actually observed.

Related to tonight's #99/#101 deploy work but a distinct pre-existing bug (from #97), not something
those PRs touch.
EOF

gh pr create --fill --base main --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
## Summary

Forcing a replace on the substrate VM tonight (to pick up cloud-init changes without waiting for a
future natural replacement) failed: `Invalid resource usage: 'External IP address: ... is already
in-use.'`. The instance's only external IP is the fixed `substrate` Address, intentionally reused
across replacements so DNS survives them — but that means Pulumi's default create-before-delete
strategy can never work for this resource; a static external IP can't be attached to two instances
at once.

## Change

`deleteBeforeReplace: true` on the instance. Trades a moment of downtime during any future replace
for one that actually succeeds — acceptable for what's already a stateless container host (state
lives in Cloud SQL / Secret Manager, not on the VM).

input.command:
cat > /tmp/pr-100-consolidated.md << 'EOF'
## Summary

Everything from tonight's work getting the people-hub/Directus deploy live for the first time,
consolidated into one PR (was split across #100-#106; squashed into this one on request).

- **Admin bootstrap trigger fix (#99):** cloud-init now tears down containers from any other
  compose project before bringing its own up — the pre-substrate-rename `portal` project was never
  torn down and held ports 80/443, plausibly interrupting Directus mid-bootstrap before it seeded
  the admin user. Extracted the cloud-init string-templating into a pulumi-free
  `substrate-bootstrap-script.ts` so it's unit testable.
- **Secret ordering:** `getSecretVersionOutput` for the admin bootstrap password now `dependsOn`
  the secret's own `SecretVersion` write — no implicit ordering existed before.
- **Schema version mismatch (#101):** `schema.yaml`'s recorded `directus: 11.17.4` didn't match the
  pinned `12.3.1` image, so `/schema/diff` always 400'd. Bumped to `12.3.1` — verified the schema
  content itself was already compatible.
- **`crm.<domain>` -> `directus.<domain>`:** Directus is the data layer's admin screen, not a
  customer-facing CRM surface. Renamed the subdomain, DNS record, compose env var
  (`CRM_DOMAIN` -> `DIRECTUS_DOMAIN`, including a spot in `docker-compose.yml` missed in the first
  pass), and internal identifiers to match.
- **`app_access` bug:** `DirectusRole` never set `app_access` on the policies it creates, so every
  role defaulted to API-only access — real users could authenticate fine but got "No App Access"
  the moment the Data Studio itself checked the token. Made `appAccess` a required field (no
  default, given this was exactly a silent-default bug) — `true` for Staff/Coach, `false` for
  Guardian (no login path yet).
- **VM replace fixes:** the substrate VM's only external IP is a fixed `Address` reused across
  replacements (so DNS survives them) — that means a normal create-before-delete replace can never
  work. Added `deleteBeforeReplace: true`. Also moved the VM from `us-west1-a` to `us-west1-b` after
  hitting a real `e2-medium` capacity shortage in `-a` mid-replace tonight (a live outage, already
  fixed in production; this just tracks it in git).

## Test plan

- [x] `just ci` passes.
- [x] New unit tests for the compose-project cleanup ordering.
- [x] Verified live end-to-end tonight: admin bootstrap succeeds, schema/roles/your-account all
      deploy, `directus.cycsail.team` serves Directus with a working admin login (`app_access`
      fixed), portal still healthy on the same static IP after the VM move.
- [x] Schema-version and `app_access` fixes were each verified by hand against real local Directus
      12.3.1 containers before being applied live (see individual commit messages for exact repro
      steps).

Fixes #99. Fixes #101.
EOF
gh pr edit 100 --title "Fix Directus admin bootstrap, schema version, domain, app_access, and VM replace" --body-file /tmp/pr-100-consolidated.md

still pending, so this fails loudly on the next deploy instead of
silently reporting success. Extracted the REST client (httpFetch,
waitForReachable, login, directusRequest, applySchema) into a
pulumi-free directus-client.ts so this is actually unit testable -
directus.ts's own module-level code constructs real GCP resources on
import, same reason substrate-bootstrap-script.ts exists.
EOF
)"
